nonmatching_review.CInt64_Mul: Same instruction operations and call order; differing nonoverlapping stack temporary slots. All sign cases yield modulo-2**64 multiplication.
nonmatching_review.CInt64_MulU: Same shift-and-add algorithm. Registers and scheduling differ. First loop adds rhs shifted by lhs low-word bits; second adds high-word cross product modulo 2**32.
nonmatching_review.CInt64_IsInRange: Same signed bounds for widths1/2/4/8, invalid widths return false. Both operands XOR the high sign bit before unsigned comparison; negative values compare >=signed lower bound, nonnegative <=signed upper bound. Stack allocation and inline comparison scheduling differ. Two switch tables unresolved; no exact claim.
nonmatching_review.CInt64_DivMod: Native64-step restoring unsigned division. Zero divisor returns without writing outputs; optional quotient/remainder outputs respected. Same carry shifts, unsigned >=test and modular subtraction through Add plus complemented divisor+1. Register permutation ECX/EDX and one extra spill/reload remain; no exact claim.

reviewed_equivalent_functions.name: InitializeIncludeCache
reviewed_equivalent_functions.memory_writes: Sets freelist=0, cachelist=freelist, availablecache=0x800000. Target explicitly reloads freelist after writing zero; compiled output propagates the known zero into cachelist directly. Both write the same three global words in the same order.
reviewed_equivalent_functions.difference: Equivalent zero propagation; no required return value (original STABS FUN returns void). No volatile casts or assembly used to force a match.
reviewed_equivalent_functions.review_status: Equivalent under the original single-threaded cache initialization contract. Does not establish equivalence under asynchronous inspection between individual machine instructions.

reviewed_equivalent_functions.name: CleanupIncludeCache
reviewed_equivalent_functions.branches: Walks active cache list, then freelist. Saves next pointer before each deallocation. Active entry text pointer is tested for NULL; null text skips both handle and allocation release.
reviewed_equivalent_functions.external_calls: For each non-null active text: OS_FreeHandle(text) then xfree(text). Then xfree(entry). For every freelist entry: xfree(entry). Finally InitializeIncludeCache(). Both xfree and OS_FreeHandle use their observed callee-cleaned calling conventions.
reviewed_equivalent_functions.memory_writes: No cache entry is read after its allocation is freed. State reset is delegated to InitializeIncludeCache. Same external call order and arguments as the target.
reviewed_equivalent_functions.difference: Register allocation in equivalent pointer loads and list traversal; target and compiled bodies have identical length and call/branch structure. Both preserve EBX and ESI.

reviewed_equivalent_functions.name: CacheIncludeFile
reviewed_equivalent_functions.external_calls: Starts with OS_GetHandleSize(text,&size); both ignore its status. Releases an evicted text with OS_FreeHandle(text), xfree(text), then sets its pointer to NULL. Calls deletecacheentry before linking the victim into freelist. Calls makecacheentry for replacement, OS_GetMilliseconds for timestamp, then insertcacheentry.
reviewed_equivalent_functions.pinned_case: If precompiled is nonzero, searches for the first entry with nonzero precompiled, regardless of locked count. If present, releases its text, deletes it from cachelist, and prepends it to freelist. Does not increase availablecache for that victim. The inserted precompiled entry also does not decrease availablecache.
reviewed_equivalent_functions.ordinary_case: If precompiled is zero and size>0x800000, returns immediately without allocation or list mutation. Otherwise while size>availablecache, scans entries for locked==0 AND precompiled==0, selecting the unsigned-smallest when value. If no eligible entry exists, returns without inserting. Each selected victim's text is released, availablecache increases by victim.size, and the entry is recycled. Repeats until enough budget exists.
reviewed_equivalent_functions.memory_writes: New/reused entry gets locked=1, precompiled=zero-extended input byte, exactly 0x204 file-spec bytes copied to offset0x14, text pointer at0x10, size at0x218, timestamp at0x21c. insertcacheentry updates next/prev and list head. Only ordinary inserted entries subtract size from availablecache.
reviewed_equivalent_functions.difference: Equivalent branch arrangement and register allocation; compiled body is eight bytes shorter. No semantics-changing shortcuts were used to increase score. All ordinary/pinned, eligible/ineligible victim, exhausted-budget and empty-list branches were checked against the target assembly and decompilation.

reviewed_equivalent.name: Browser_PackBrowseFile
reviewed_equivalent.branches: Null browsedata reports assertion at line0xfe; null browsetable reports at line0xff. Assertions may return and both implementations continue. Allocation error prints the exact diagnostic to stderr and exits(-23) without returning. Successful allocation continues serialization and returns1.
reviewed_equivalent.header: 40-byte header: magic DubL, version1, host-endianness byte derived from integer1, sixteen zero padding bytes, count truncated to16bits, browse_data_offset=40, browse_data_length=OS_GetHandleSize result, file_data_offset=(datasize+47)&~7, file_data_length=CalcDiskSpaceRequirements result.
reviewed_equivalent.handle_calls: Calls OS_GetHandleSize on the OS handle instead of the obsolete Memory handle wrapper. Locks table via GetBrowseTableInfoAndLock to calculate serialized size, then unlocks it. Allocates totalSize=tableSize+tableOffset via OS_NewHandle and stores the resulting two-word handle to the output argument before checking its error status. Locks the output with MsDos_GetValidMemBufferPtr.
reviewed_equivalent.memory_writes: Copies exactly40headerbytes to output. Locks browsedata, copies datasizebytes to output+40, zeroes bytes up to alignedtableOffset, then unlocks browsedata. Locks browsetable again, serializes entries with ConvertMemToDisk at output+tableOffset, zeroes any remaining allocated tail, unlocks browsetable and output. Sizes, padding expressions and output pointer positions agree with target instructions.
reviewed_equivalent.differences: Register allocation, local spill/stack slot layout and expression scheduling. Source uses equivalent natural serialized-header field order and a separate temporary for the locked data pointer. No inline assembly, volatile casts or altered failure behavior were introduced to raise the score.
reviewed_equivalent.scope: Reviewed equivalence for the observed OS-handle ABI and valid input sizes. This is not exhaustive execution-based validation over corrupted handles or arbitrary machine states.

branch_conditions: Select last token only when numargtoks > 0; enter coalescing only if last exists, last.kind == 2, and last.text[0] == 0.
Compute fourth/third/previous pointers only for counts > 3, > 2, > 1 respectively; continue only if previous exists.
If incoming kind == 1, previous.kind in {4,5}, and (third.kind != 2 || fourth.kind != 3), optionally log, subtract two from numargtoks, and replace incoming kind with previous.kind.
Otherwise, if previous.kind == 1 and incoming kind in {4,5}, optionally log and subtract two from numargtoks.
If numargtoks >= maxargtoks, grow allocation by sixteen records; initialize the next record and increment numargtoks.
memory_writes: xrealloc("argument list", argtoks, (maxargtoks + 16) << 3); store returned pointer; maxargtoks += 16.
Write 16-bit entry.kind; store xstrdup(text) if non-null, otherwise NULL; numargtoks++.
The coalescing paths overwrite prior slots by moving the count backward, retaining the original behavior and ownership semantics.
calls_and_errors: Arg_GetTokenName(previous), printf with the original two coalescing messages, gated by parserDebug alias data_00588519.
Allocation and duplication retain original xrealloc/xstrdup stdcall ABI and failure behavior; no added error calls.
input_cases: Empty and non-empty token lists; last kind other than 2; empty versus non-empty last text.
Incoming kinds 1,4,5 and other signed short values; previous kinds 1,4,5 and other values; third/fourth exclusion pair.
Debug flag zero/nonzero; allocation below/at capacity; input text NULL/non-NULL.
Arg_AddToken.remaining_codegen_differences: Register allocation and signed-word promotion/range-check lowering; shared decrement versus duplicate decrement paths. The observable branches, calls, stores, and return are preserved.
Arg_AddToken.limits: Review assumes the original parser invariants and defined inputs. The original conditional accesses of third/fourth and last.text are preserved; this port does not claim to repair invalid token state.

branch_conditions: Loop while Arg_GotMore(); obtain Arg_GetNext(1); stop if it returns NULL.

Recognize a leading option prefix only if the argument has at least two characters and its first character is in FIRSTARGCHAR alias data_00587eec. Preserve pending end-of-argument emission and option flag transitions.

For backslash followed by any of the three configured separator bytes, consume the next character and set its high bit. In compatibility mode 1 only, protect a colon immediately followed by backslash by setting the high bit.
For a non-separator character, clear the high bit when its low seven bits equal a configured separator, append to the buffer, and report overflow when the output pointer reaches buffer + 0x1000.

For a separator, emit an option token when the option flag is set, then text token, then kind 5 for comma, kind 4 for equals/SEP3, otherwise kind 0. Reset the buffer and option flag as in the original.

At argument end, emit option/text slices with the same optional prefix skip when flagA and nonempty buffer; otherwise emit text and end-of-argument tokens. Emit a final end-of-argument when flagA or flagB remains, then kind 0.
memory_writes: Local 4096-byte buffer and its terminators; local option/separator flags and source/output cursors.
Persistent token state changes only through the same Arg_AddToken calls, with the same kind and text arguments.
calls_and_errors: Arg_GotMore, Arg_GetNext(1), strchr for configured option prefixes, Arg_AddToken in the same semantic order.
CLPReportError(2, tok, tok + strlen(tok) - 15, 0x1000) at the same buffer threshold; retains original behavior if the reporter returns.
input_cases: Empty argument, one-character argument, option prefix with/without following text, option slices with or without a second prefix.
Each separator byte, comma/equals distinctions, escaped separators, ordinary backslashes, mode-1 drive-colon followed by backslash, and modes other than 1.
NULL next argument, exhausted input, buffer contents below/at overflow threshold, pending option and separator flags.
Arg_Parse.remaining_codegen_differences: Equivalent byte OR/AND assignments use common-subexpression elimination and different branch sharing; buf + 1 + i versus an equivalent buffer slice expression changes address arithmetic. Signed char conversions and short token-kind calls were checked against original instructions.
Arg_Parse.limits: No dynamic execution equivalence test was performed. Manual review covers decoded control flow and data flow; original overflow-reporting semantics are retained.

branch_conditions: Kind 2 returns token.text directly; kind 3 returns "option"; kind 5 returns "comma".
Kind 4 returns "colon or equals" for compatibility == 1, otherwise "equals".
Kind 1 returns "end of argument"; kind 0 returns "end of command line"; all remaining signed short kinds return "<error>".
input_cases: All 65536 signed-short token-kind bit patterns partition into 0,1,2,3,4,5,other.
All compatibility-byte values partition into exactly 1 versus all others; the compatibility byte is loaded once only on the relevant branch.
Kind 2 may return NULL text unchanged; token pointer validity follows the original precondition.
Arg_GetTokenName.remaining_codegen_differences: The target materializes the first compound boolean in EDX and then tests it; the candidate branches directly on the same predicates. Return strings and the direct text pointer are identical.
Arg_GetTokenName.limits: Manual exhaustive predicate partition review; no writes or error paths exist.
